builds.name: Shuriken/Butterfly Playstyle
builds.summary: Q: Alchemical Vapor, E: Shuriken, R: Butterfly/Skylark, T: Mark of Death. Recommended to start and learn with this build.
builds.forWhom: Recommended to start and learn with this build.

builds.name: No Ult Playstyle
builds.summary: Q: Alchemical Vapor, E: Shuriken, R: Butterfly/Skylark, T: Bomb (Great Thunderbolt). Trades the ultimate's 1v1 pressure and reliable kill securing for AoE CC that buffs the whole team's damage (20% vs heroes, 30% vs units), one extra invisibility charge, and a 4-reset-vs-3-reset cooldown-economy edge. The source itself calls this post "a bit out-dated" relative to the newer Bomb+Shuri recommendation - the RECOMMENDATION direction (bomb over ult) is current, but framing it as a distinct alternative build is slightly stale. ""Bomb is More Risk, More Snowball but More Potential Rewards while being also more Flop Potential too.""
builds.forWhom: Weaker into choke-point fights, 1v1 duels, and CCi-diver classes (Nodachi, Poleaxe).

builds.name: No Butterfly Playstyle
builds.summary: "Strongest skillcap & impact high lobby." Q: Alchemical Vapor, E: Shuriken, R: Bomb (Great Thunderbolt), T: Skylark or Butterfly in a hero-kill-favorable meta, otherwise Mark of Death.
builds.forWhom: Recommended only if confident - start with this if trusting yourself to learn the playstyle.

builds.name: Duo DB
builds.summary: Team-comp note, not a solo build: when playing two Dual Blades together (Amya cites her own GRK duo), having one player run no-ult and the other run the ultimate can outperform both running the ultimate; the split can also flex mid-match (swapping shuriken for bomb on one player, or both going no-ult in low-skirmish games).

matchups.vs: Musket and similar squishy ranged heroes without dedicated HP investment
matchups.why: musket.md (cross-class): players invest HP to "avoid dying to a single DB/CD combo" and "make it so enemy DB/CD can't kill u in 1 combo anymore." [unverified: named from the Musket side, not corroborated by a DB-side matchup list]

Which of the two DB ultimates (Marked for Death vs The Dance of Death) is unspecified. [unverified: ultimate not specified]

matchups.why: "against CCi-Divers classes like Nodachi or Poleaxe" the ultimate's pressure/reliability is missed most.

single narrated clip (knightstalker VOD, 2022): stopping "this Dual Blades unit from blocking the point" - suggests a stationary DB hero on a point is vulnerable to sustained poison/ranged fire. [unverified: single incidental data point, not a stated doctrine]

techniques.name: Animation canceling
steps: Training room: try roll-canceling, dismount-canceling and blocking on every skill to learn which are cancelable.
techniques.rhythm: Amya: EVERY CLASS CAN DO IT! - Blocking is the primary cancel; roll canceling interrupts full spells, dismounts, and creates movement otherwise impossible. Costs extra stamina.

techniques.name: Active blocking
steps: it can be BROKEN and stagger you
techniques.rhythm: Don't get "Block checked" - Being an active blocker prevents undesired skills landing on you.

techniques.name: Horse-whistle CC immunity
steps: Time the whistle on the enemy CC
you take damage but no CC
techniques.rhythm: bugs out with PIN/LOCK skills, so care

techniques.name: Walk into braced units
steps: Walk (don't sprint) into their minimal range
techniques.rhythm: brace damage scales with your speed towards them - For braced units like Forte, Halberds, Phalanx - niche: enemy hero outnumbered, unaware or afk.

techniques.name: Q-spell invis-window timing
steps: cast the Q-spell (Alchemical Vapours) from any invisibility window
always at the very end of that window

techniques.name: Horse-mount free invisibility
steps: grants a free invisibility window plus 200% move speed for 3 seconds
techniques.rhythm: distinct mobility/escape tool from Alchemical Vapours - Separate from, and stackable with, the universal horse-whistle CC-immune summon-animation trick.

gameplay.text: To master DB is to master the entire game. You'll have a brutal learning curve, but mastering DB means mastering the game.

The dual blades are a pair of daggers suitable for assassination missions. Appropriately, dual blades users have excellent mobility, invisibility, and single-target damage, and excel at hunting down and killing enemy heroes. They are, however, very lackluster against units and fare poorly against coordinated groups of enemies.

positioning.intro: Where to be during a fight ("golden diagonal" win-condition doctrine):

bullets.text: Final point cap.
Point near the final point - one cap.

bullets.lead: Canceling supply on B fight reset/during the fight:
bullets.text: delaying the resetup, canceling the 2 units strats is enough for your team to get B.

bullets.lead: Cap supply and get units out of it -
bullets.text: then either stay on it if you want to win by B, or go one of the 2 points you are pressuring.
Pressure enough people for your team to have number advantages, dont feel forced to fight if it's the case.

Move a unit that can kill afk units in map border (there is a lot), and start your plan JUST BEFORE YOUR TEAM ENGAGE ON B (then worst case you will bait people out of B fight and make pressure), NOT DURING AS PEOPLE WILL RESPAWN.
Final point / Point near final point / Supply.
"As a DB it's IMPOSSIBLE to die if you don't try to fight and just play safe. By playing around this golden diagonal, you have all the winconditions I quoted a top."
Don't sprint-AA unless needed. Use normal walk + roll cancel for DPS.
"Kick > Ambush (nearly same damage, but Kick stuns and have highen pen)" - preference note between the two combo terms that don't map to a confirmed wiki skill name.
to play slow and play around cooldowns.
Test your mobility in Custom, what you can do or not do.
Always engage with spells that keep escape options open.
Learn enemy spell cooldowns - bait them, punish greed.
Know every map/object hitbox - use the environment to survive.
Movement is survival - every duel is winnable with good spacing.
Autoattacks matter - squeezing AA will be a huge difference in DPS.
Stay active. You should ALWAYS be looking to catch heroes, help dps units.
treated as non-negotiable across every build variant - it is the only cleanse of crowd control the class has.

bullets.lead: Butterfly over Skylark once the epic schematic is equipped:
bullets.text: Butterfly's burst/overall damage is higher and it benefits more from on-kill spell resets, even though Skylark's lower cooldown makes it the easier starting pick for new players.

a Dual Blades player's job is to consistently trade for "more than 1 person" of value - via player trades, supply-blocking (added value for every player it distracts without a hero kill needed), cavalry-flank feint pressure (sometimes the threat alone, without committing, is the highest-value play), and generally forcing the enemy team to divert attention/resources.

Chaindart's OP describes a common rotation where a player swaps INTO Chaindart temporarily for its supply-defense utility window, "then swapping back to another class (LB or DB for example)." This frames Dual Blades as a class players return to, not one they routinely swap away from mid-fight.

bullets.lead: House note on Strength vs Agility (top authority):
bullets.text: "Yes, the problem is the weapon can't reach 2k pene, maybe if you put some agility and have really good rolls in weapon, putting some agility will make you go to the soft cap of pene if not full str." Full Strength stays the default pick (matches Amya), but the class's slashing-penetration ceiling is hard to reach on Strength alone without excellent gear rolls, which is why some players mix in Agility to hit the soft cap instead. ([IM] Kazepos, Immortals #heroes, 28/01/2026 - marked status: likely-stale in the source capture, predates the 22/06/2026 patch anchor)
